title: How can five even numbers in a row be written from the middle one?
description: Five even numbers are in a row and the middle one is five p. The video steps down and up from the middle, two at a time, to name the other four, and checks with a sample value. The method is the same as the example in the book on numbers in a row.
teaching_notes: One idea: even numbers in a row go up by two, so each step from the middle adds or takes away two. Watch for students who step by one and write five p plus one, as for ordinary numbers in a row.

source: The middle number in the sequence of 5 consecutive even number
video_script.why: A learner names even numbers in a row from the middle one, stepping by two each time.
video_script.substitution: the book's own middle number: five p
video_script.anchor: five number cards in a row, each two more than the one before, with the middle card marked 5p
video_script.payoff_line: The numbers are five p minus four, five p minus two and five p. Then come five p plus two and five p plus four.

final_answer.spoken: the numbers are five p minus four, five p minus two and five p, then five p plus two and five p plus four

maths_rules: even numbers in a row differ by 2
two below the middle: 5p - 2; two below that: 5p - 4
two above the middle: 5p + 2; two above that: 5p + 4
check with p = 2: middle 10, then 6, 8, 10, 12, 14; each is 2 more than the one before and there are five
video_script.design: One idea: from the middle, go down two and up two, twice each way. Assumes the example on numbers in a row. The five cards stay on the board with the middle card marked 5p.

beats.on_screen: title card Even Numbers in a Row; five blank cards stand in a row like steps of a staircase; the middle card is marked 5p

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the five blank cards line up
marks.mid: the middle card glows and is marked five p
marks.ask: a question mark glows over the other four cards

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about five even numbers in a row.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>The middle one is five p. We will solve it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we write the other four numbers using p?

beats.on_screen: the five cards stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: five cards in a row; an arrow between each pair of neighbours is marked +2

marks.even: the cards two, four, six and eight light up as even numbers in a row
marks.step: each arrow between neighbours is marked plus two

narration: <bookmark mark='even'/>Even numbers in a row, like two, four, six and eight, go up by two each time.
<bookmark mark='step'/>A step to the right adds two, and a step to the left takes away two.

beats.on_screen: Given: five even numbers in a row; the middle one is 5p

marks.given: the five even numbers and the middle number are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five even numbers are in a row, and the middle one is five p.

beats.on_screen: To find: the other four numbers in terms of p
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write the other four numbers using p.

marks.two: the card left of the middle shows five p minus two
marks.four: the first card shows five p minus four

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step one, go left from the middle. The next even number is two less, so it is five p minus two.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Two less again gives five p minus four, and that is the first card.

marks.two: the card right of the middle shows five p plus two
marks.four: the last card shows five p plus four

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, go right from the middle. The next even number is two more, so it is five p plus two.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Two more again gives five p plus four, and that is the last card.

marks.put: two is put in for p and the middle card shows ten
marks.row: the cards show six, eight, ten, twelve and fourteen, each two more than the one before

narration: <bookmark mark='put'/>Step three, put the answer back with p as two. The middle number five p is ten.
<bookmark mark='row'/>The cards show six, eight, ten, twelve and fourteen. Each is two more than the one before, so the check works.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The numbers are five p minus four, five p minus two and five p. Then come five p plus two and five p plus four.
